{{< include _head.qmd >}}

Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov's harmony textbook was first published in St Petersburg in 1886. It teaches modulation through short
four-voice progressions, and these are its modulation examples: each starts in C major or A minor and reaches a new key, a few go there and back. They
are grouped by the book's example number; the letters are its variants.

How to read the labels and use the scores: [Analysed Scores](index.qmd#reading-the-labels). For modulation itself, see
[Chapter 22](../modulation.qmd).

{{< include _rimsky-korsakov-harmony.qmd >}}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## For teachers

- **Source:** the notes and analyses are the DDMAL Key Modulation Dataset's encodings of the book's examples (Néstor Nápoles López and
  others), translated automatically to RomanText and copied into When in Rome. `scripts/when-in-rome/build.mjs` reads the MusicXML
  (`src/rimsky`), and every note was checked against music21's reading of the same files.
- **Example numbers** are the dataset's (3-5a and so on; the 3 is dropped here). They have not been checked against a printed edition.
- **Not edited:** the analyses are an automated translation and are shown as they are.
:::
